questions.text: Have some more tea, _____ ?
questions.textHindi: Have some more tea, _____ ?
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) won't you (B) must you (C) can you (D) should you
Question tags for invitations or friendly offers use "won't you".

questions.text: The rise and fall of the tide _____ due to lunar influence.
questions.textHindi: The rise and fall of the tide _____ due to lunar influence.
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) are (B) is (C) were (D) have
"The rise and fall" represents a single collective phenomenon, taking a singular verb.

questions.text: The children locked _____ up in the cupboard.
questions.textHindi: The children locked _____ up in the cupboard.
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) their (B) himself (C) them (D) themselves

questions.text: The synonym of 'Concealed' is
questions.textHindi: The synonym of 'Concealed' is
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) Covered (B) Sealed (C) Closed (D) Hidden

questions.text: The antonym of 'Urban' is
questions.textHindi: The antonym of 'Urban' is
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) Rustic (B) Rural (C) Civil (D) Foreign
"Urban" refers to cities, whereas "Rural" refers to the countryside.

questions.text: 'To make both ends meet' means
questions.textHindi: 'To make both ends meet' means
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) to buy costly articles (B) to live within one's income (C) live a luxurious life (D) to please all people

questions.text: He declared his _____
questions.textHindi: He declared his _____

questions.text: They were surprised _____ hear him sing.
questions.textHindi: They were surprised _____ hear him sing.

Options: (A) by (B) to (C) at (D) of

questions.text: He has properly _____ the rules and regulations.
questions.textHindi: He has properly _____ the rules and regulations.
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) understand (B) to understand (C) understood (D) understanding

questions.text: _____ a borrower nor a lender be.
questions.textHindi: _____ a borrower nor a lender be.
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) Either (B) Nor (C) Neither (D) Or

questions.text: India is progressing _____
questions.textHindi: India is progressing _____
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) by leaps and bounds (B) by fits and starts (C) by body and soul (D) by hook or by crook
"By leaps and bounds" is an idiom meaning very rapidly.

questions.text: I want to take _____ classes this year.
questions.textHindi: I want to take _____ classes this year.
questions.explanationHindi:
Options: (A) less (B) little (C) fewer (D) any

questions.textHindi: The cat is hiding _____ the bed.

b) Justice was tolerably fair. The ordinary rule was to avoid courts.

a) The voice of my education said to me / He must be killed
b) Can you, that I lived in such a house and / Was proud, and loved
c) There shall be / In that rich earth a richer dust concealed ; / A dust whom England bore, shaped, made aware
d) Nurses to the graves are gone, / And the prams go rolling on.
[Answer for Option c]
Context: These lines are excerpted from Rupert Brooke's famous war sonnet "The Soldier".
Explanation: The poet expresses profound patriotic devotion to his homeland, England. He reflects that if he dies on a foreign battlefield, that small plot of foreign earth will forever contain an English essence—his body, which was nurtured, shaped, and enlightened by England. It symbolizes eternal gratitude and love for one's motherland.

viii) हमें पेड़ लगाना चाहिए ।

List-B: a) Martin Luther King, Jr., b) Bertrand Russell, c) Dr. Zakir Hussain, d) Dorothy L. Sayers, e) Shiga Naoya
[Answers/Solutions for Q6 parts]
[Summary of Indian Civilization and Culture (b-iii)]
"Indian Civilization and Culture" is an essay written by Mahatma Gandhi. In this essay, Gandhiji contrasts Indian civilization with Western civilization. He points out that Indian civilization is founded on moral elevation, self-discipline, and duty, whereas Western civilization is driven by materialism and the multiplication of wants. Gandhiji emphasizes that while western civilization promotes bodily comforts, Indian civilization encourages the mastery over mind and passions. He argues that our ancestors correctly dissuaded us from luxuries and corruption, ensuring our culture has withstood the test of time.
[Notes for 6c - English as a second language of India (OR option)]
English occupies a unique and vital position in India as an associate official language and a second language. Inherited from the British colonial administration, English has deeply integrated into India's legal, educational, administrative, and technological frameworks. It acts as a crucial link language across linguistically diverse states, facilitating national and international communication, higher education, scientific research, and global commerce.

ii) Snake -> c) D.H. Lawrence

iv) Now the Leaves are Falling Fast -> a) W.H. Auden
v) Fire-Hymn -> d) K.N. Daruwalla

Read the passage carefully and answer the questions that follow :
[Passage: Smile tonic...]
Questions:
a) What is the best tonic for our mind and body?
b) What should we practise when we are relaxed in bed?
c) What should we do to be cheerful?
d) What happens when we constantly think about negative things?
OR
Write a précis of the following passage and give a suitable title:
[Passage: Character of good men...]
[Answers for Reading Comprehension (Option 1)]
a) A smile is the best tonic for our mind and body.
b) When we are relaxed and in bed, we should practise putting some cheerful thoughts into our minds.
c) To be cheerful, we have to create positive thoughts.
d) When we constantly think about negative things, we feel unhappy.
[Précis for Option 2]
Title: The Virtue of Good Men
Précis: Good men, akin to selfless trees, live for others and uphold their righteous principles regardless of praise or adversity. Unlike selfish individuals who live merely for personal desires, those who sacrifice themselves for the welfare of others attain eternal bliss and remembrance.
